official_scoring_source.formula: final_mse * max(0.1, measured_flops / budget_flops), mean across MLPs; failures use multiplier 1.0

conventions.sd: sample SD with denominator n-1 across networks
conventions.quantiles: Hyndman-Fan type 7 / linear interpolation with h=(n-1)p
conventions.worst_fraction: sort descending by adjusted score; n=100 means exact top 10 and top 25

cost_vs_mse_variation.conclusion: Across these 100 rows the compute multiplier is constant, so cost variation contributes zero to cross-network score dispersion; adjusted-score dispersion is exactly the scaled MSE dispersion.

interpretation.basis: Worst 10% contribute 12.47% rather than a dominant fraction; worst 25% contribute 29.31%; largest single row is 1.36%. The bulk 90% still contributes 87.53% of total score.
interpretation.global_research_implication: Large score reductions require a globally applicable mechanism that moves the center and broad bulk of the MSE distribution, not special treatment of a few high-error networks. Evaluation should track central quantiles and tail regressions under one fixed global method/configuration with no per-network selection.

limitations: Descriptive development evidence only on R209 public mini:all-100.
No leaderboard comparison, rank, or same-panel external gap is inferred.
Network-level descriptive SE is not a held-out significance guarantee.
No estimator, Actions, new data access, paid/private/holdout/full evaluation, tuning, submission, model, leaderboard, or canonical edit.
